Subject: Performance SLO — Private/VPC network follow-up

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and next steps from Redwood's side so we have a single reference:

Summary of customer targets we captured on the call:
- End-to-end p95 latency target: <= 120 ms (goal); p99 <= 250 ms
- Streaming requirement: sub-100 ms first-byte on streaming responses, and per-token pacing ~20 ms for interactive sessions
- Throughput: sustained baseline ~100k tokens/minute, with burst ability to 300k tokens/minute during peak windows
- Concurrency: support for ~500 sustained concurrent sessions, bursting to ~2,000 concurrent sessions

Networking/architecture notes we need from Acme to qualify private/VPC options:
1) Preferred connectivity model: VPC Peering, Transit Gateway peering, or AWS PrivateLink?
2) Egress path and NAT/Proxy details (NAT Gateway, egress through corporate FW, or direct internet egress)
3) Typical internal app-to-inference latency (ms) inside the VPC (measurements are helpful)
4) Any bandwidth or egress cost constraints we should be aware of

What Redwood will provide next:
- A short SLO matrix + recommended network checklist (attached)
- Sample test commands (iperf/traceroute) for SRE to run toward our endpoints
- Options and guidance for peering vs PrivateLink based on throughput/latency needs

Can you share the network diagram and the contact for your SRE team so we can loop them in? If it helps, Jordan can run through the technical runbook next week — I propose Wed 2027-06-09 at 10:00am PT.

Attachments: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx (xlsx) — SLO matrix and checklist

Thanks — look forward to the next steps.

—Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.com

Hey Marissa — great summary, appreciate the clear SLOs. A few quick notes from our side and answers to your questions:

- Connectivity: we're currently on AWS (us-west-2) using a Transit Gateway topology. We typically prefer TGW peering for high-throughput services but can evaluate PrivateLink if latency looks significantly better.
- Egress: production egress currently goes through a NAT Gateway in our shared services VPC and then out through a managed firewall. Egress costs are a factor but latency is the bigger concern here.
- Internal latency: measured app -> shared-services VPC ~35-40 ms on average; app -> external vendor endpoints (internet) varies but often 80-200 ms depending on route.
- Bandwidth: we have 10 Gbps links available on the TGW side; sustained usage in the 200-300 Mbps range so far for ML inference traffic.

I'm attaching our high-level network topology diagram (acme-network-topology.png) — that should help. Our SRE team (sre@acme-corp.com) is copied here and can run tests if you provide the exact endpoints and preferred test methodology.

Wed 2027-06-09 10:00am PT works for me as a tentative slot — Jordan/Vivek, are you available?

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Senior Engineering Manager, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme-corp.com
Attachment: acme-network-topology.png

Hi Jordan/Marissa — SRE here. Thanks for the checklist — a few notes from a setup perspective and what we can provide:

- Current infra: Transit Gateway (TGW) with TGW attachments to our app VPCs. Egress through NAT Gateway and centralized firewall cluster.
- Measured latency: app -> shared-services VPC ~28-40 ms; to external vendor endpoints (public internet) often >100 ms depending on path. We can run baseline traceroutes/iperf to the IPs you provide.
- Throughput: our TGW path supports up to 10 Gbps; we can dedicate bandwidth if needed but would prefer to understand sustained vs burst requirements first.

Connectivity options we can support: TGW peering (preferred for high throughput), AWS PrivateLink (lower maintenance but may require NLB fronting and has per-GB costs). We're open to either depending on the recommended approach.

Requested items from Redwood to proceed:
- List of endpoint IPs/CIDR and expected ports (TCP 443, 8443, any UDP?)
- Preferred test commands (please provide iperf/traceroute commands and sample expected outputs)
- ETA for when tape-up or dedicated peering would be required if we need a production SLA

Attached: vpc-peering-request-form.pdf (pdf) and network-test-instructions.txt with suggested commands. We'll run tests this week and upload results to the Drive link.

Thanks,
